messages:
kim: FYI customer reported parser failures when using response_format=json + strict=true. They hit 422 parsing error even though payload looks valid. Repro steps attached.

chris: customer says it started after a deploy this morning, intermittent. they pasted a snippet: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"...","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```

kim: captured response body from their run: 
```
)]}',
{"result": {"answer": "42"}}

or sometimes:
<!doctype html>
<html>...error page...

headers: 
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 312
x-request-id: req_abc123
```

javier: weird — leading characters like `)]}',` will definitely break strict JSON. Also if the upstream returned an HTML error page the content-type mismatch will cause enforcement to reject. Do we have the runtime logs for req_abc123?

priya: adding context from model side: when the model runtime falls back to a fast-safe stub (due to OOM/latency), the error handler returns an HTML debug page on 500. We should not surface that through the API when response_format=json is requested.

maya: customer reported latency spikes ~700-900ms right before failures. Could be a capacity fallback to lighter variant.

kim: attached runtime response logs for req_abc123 (redacted): 
```
2026-03-17T09:14:12Z INFO request start req_abc123 user=acct-9
2026-03-17T09:14:12Z ERROR model group gpt-xl shard-2 OOM -> fallback to stub; returning 500 html page
2026-03-17T09:14:13Z INFO response sent status=200 body_len=45 content-type=text/html req_abc123
```

ops-bot: Notifying eng-runtime oncall group... @eng-runtime

javier: mitigation options: 1) short-term: sanitize responses before enforcement — strip common prefixes like `)]}',` and treat text/html with heuristic JSON extraction only for non-strict clients; 2) immediate customer workaround: add `Accept: application/json` header and set `strict=false` in request to bypass enforcement; 3) longer-term: runtime should never return HTML for 200 responses when response_format=json is set.

priya: agree. For repro, try this curl that mimics the customer's headers: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"ping","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```

kim: i reproduced locally without Accept header and got the broken prefix. With Accept: application/json the runtime returned a clean JSON 200.

maya: escalation created ENG-12345, priority P2. tagging eng-runtime and infra for triage. suggested rollback window if deploy was the trigger.

javier: dev notes for eng-runtime: enforce content-type on server-side handler earlier; if strict=true always validate content-type==application/json and if not, return 422 with structured error rather than HTML. Also log fallback reasons prominently.

priya: i'll push a small guard into the runtime handler to drop HTML error pages for response_format=json and instead emit a structured error payload. will test in staging.

kim: customer accepted workaround (set Accept header + temporary strict=false). they've been notified and asked to retest. keeping this thread open until eng confirms fix in prod. :thumbsup:

chris: thanks team — please update ticket when deployed.
